thread:
anna (oncall): Paging — p99 streaming stalls and SLO breaches on dedicated-pool-9. Dashboard shows p99 jump from 300ms -> 4.2s for streaming responses starting ~6525012200. Queue depth for pool-9 at 00:30 UTC spiked to 820 (usual 40). Suspect autoscaler warmup delay + handshake cold starts. tagging @pagerduty and @toni.

mike (eng-runtime): seeing the same on traces. Lots of `stall: last_token > 5s` entries for streams. Can we confirm if autoscaler created new slots but warmup didn't complete?

sara (eng-sre): autoscaler logs show HEALTHY -> PROVISIONING -> RUNNING but handshake timeout at ~45s repeatedly. Warmup handshake liveness failing on kernel probe. Logs: ```
# tail -n 100 /var/log/autoscaler/pool-9.log
6525012190 PROVISIONING slot-128 request_id=abc..\n6525012225 HANDSHAKE_FAILED slot-128 reason=kv_cache_miss_and_kernel_probe_timeout
6525012230 PROVISIONING slot-129 request_id=def..\n6525012260 HANDSHAKE_FAILED slot-129 reason=handshake-heartbeat-missed
6525012305 RUNNING slot-130
```
Handshakes succeed rarely which causes a backlog. Queue depth + non-warmed slots => p99 tail.

toni (infra): I'm standing up manual capacity now. Increasing reserved pool count for dedicated-pool-9 by +4 as emergency. Command: ```
# infractl scale pool --pool dedicated-pool-9 --delta 4 --reason "hotshot surge, warmup failures"
```
Will also pin a fallback policy to route tenant-priority=hotshots to a prewarmed lane. Doing that next.

devon (cust-succ): Heads-up — two enterprise customers (acme-corp, delta-ads) reported streaming stalls via support. They see partial responses then stall. Customers are on high-traffic flows. Will open support tickets and send an initial status note: "We are actively mitigating; a mitigation is in progress; updates every 15m."

mike (eng-runtime): quick mitigation idea: enable temporary queue gating + priority for kv-cache-hot prefixes so prewarmed slots get first dibs. Patch gate config: ```json
{"queue_policy": "priority_first", "priority_tags": ["tenant:hotshot","prefix:kv-hot"], "max_queue_depth": 500}
```
I can deploy gate in ~5m. This will keep tail latency down for highest priority flows while we scale.

anna (oncall): deploy the gate. Also set callback so non-priority requests get 503 fast rather than stalling. We need to protect SLO for priority tenants.

sara (eng-sre): deployed gate config to pool-9. Observability: p95 improved within 120s, p99 trending down but still elevated. Current metrics snapshot: ```
p50: 90ms
p95: 420ms -> 190ms after gate
p99: 4.2s -> 1.6s (still above SLO 1s)
queue_depth: 820 -> 360
warmup_failure_rate: 38% -> 12% (after manual scale)
```
We still have intermittent streaming stalls due to a small fraction of slots repeatedly failing handshake. Need root cause for handshake failures.

toni (infra): digging into kernel probe timeouts — looks like a hotspot on image load for a particular GPU node image revision. Rolling back node image to previous revision on a subset (n=6) to test. Command: ```
# infractl nodeset update --node-group gpux-9 --image r2026-12-02 -> r2026-11-29 --count 6
```
If rollback reduces handshake failures we'll roll further.

mike (eng-runtime): meanwhile, as an additional mitigation I suggest enabling fallback routing to a slightly lower-cost model variant that is fully warmed in another pool (dedicated-pool-3). This reduces feature parity (no streaming-structured-output), but keeps latency. We can gate by tenant priority and opt-in. Thoughts?

devon (cust-succ): For acme-corp we should route them to the warmed fallback and notify them of a temporary degraded feature (no structured streaming). They prefer availability over exact feature parity. I'll coordinate a notification and rollback if they object.

anna (oncall): agreed. Toni — can you set up a routing override for tenant=acme-corp to pool-3? Tag it as emergency and TTL 45m.

toni (infra): routing override applied: ```
# routingctl override --tenant acme-corp --to-pool dedicated-pool-3 --ttl 45m --reason "emergency fallback"
```
Validation: acme stream tests now pass on fallback with p99 ~320ms.

incident-bot: Incident created: dedicated-pool-9 capacity saturation — autoscaler warmup delays. Severity: P1. Runbook: /runbooks/dedicated-warmup. Paging to oncall.

mike (eng-runtime): note — we pulled additional telemetry: KV-cache coldpath hit rate spiked to 85% during the burst which amplified warmup cost. We should consider prewarmed cache priming for hot prefixes as a medium-term fix.

anna (oncall): onboarding/hand-off: I'm handing this to mike for live mitigation and further triage. I'll remain available for customer comms. @mike please take ownership and update every 15m.

mike (eng-runtime): taking ownership. Plan: 1) stabilize with queue gating + routing overrides (done), 2) root cause handshake failures (image rollback test), 3) patch autoscaler handshake timeout to be adaptive to image load times, 4) postmortem focused on warmup playbook and prewarming recommendations. First triage update in 15m.

sara (eng-sre): FYI I've escalated to kernel/runtime team for the image load hotspot. Also flagged an autoscaler tuning ticket: AUTOSCALE-7839 to investigate heartbeat thresholds and handshake backoff.

devon (cust-succ): sent note to acme and delta-ads: "We are mitigating; you may see degraded streaming features while we route you to a warmed lane. ETA 30-45m for full mitigation." Customer replies: acme thanked us and asked for a follow-up after stabilization.

toni (infra): rollback subset nodes completed — early signal: handshake_failure_rate on nodeset gpux-9 reduced from 38% -> 4% for the rolled subset. I'm expanding rollback to remaining nodes (rolling with maxUnavailable=2).

anna (oncall): thanks team. Please keep updates in this thread. If p99 gets under 1s and queue depth < 100 for 3 consecutive min, we can start moving to monitoring mode.

mike (eng-runtime): update @6525012600: p99 is now 860ms, queue_depth 92, warmup_failure_rate 3% cluster-wide. Streaming stalls rare. Continuing to validate.

sara (eng-sre): update @6525012720: metrics holding. Will monitor for 30m then recommend incident de-escalation. Created paging note for postmortem: initial hypothesis: node image regression + aggressive autoscaler handshake timeout + high KV coldpath amplifying warmup.

devon (cust-succ): customers updated. No new support tickets in last 10m.

mike (eng-runtime): transitioning to monitoring mode. I'll create a follow-up action: AUTOFIX-2026 to add prewarm job for top-100 hot prefixes and AUTOSCALE-7839 for adaptive handshake timeouts.

anna (oncall): handing off to sara for post-incident monitoring and postmortem coordination. Thanks everyone for the quick responses. Closing live mitigation.

sara (eng-sre): taking post-incident lead. Logged actions and owners in #postmortems. We'll schedule a blameless postmortem and include recommended runbook changes: - add gate + fallback template - prewarm job for hot prefixes - autoscaler adaptive handshake step - node image canary policy for GPU images.

toni (infra): leaving a note: node image rollback fixed immediate warmup problem; we'll audit image build steps and test harness for load on first inference.
